deep.reconstruction:
Context (ff. 25r–26r): f(x) is an equation of degree m with distinct roots over a 'rationales Gebiet' S, which here means a field containing its coefficients. On f.25r, v is a Galois resolvent: a rational function of the roots taking m! distinct values. F(u) is the irreducible factor over S of degree g that v satisfies. G is the group of f over S, of order g. This page announces the program 'Allgemeine Sätze' on reducing G to a subgroup ('Divisor') G' by enlarging the base field S by S_1, so that S' = S + S_1 is the whole field of known quantities. In modern terms this is the Galois group of f over the composite field S S_1.

Two main cases are named:
(1) adjoining a single root r of an equation irreducible over S, i.e. S' = S(r);
(2) adjoining a system S_1 that is 'vollständig' over S, i.e. closed under conjugation, a normal extension. These are Galois's Propositions II and III.

Case (1) worked out:
- Over S(r), the resolvent factors as F(u) = F_1(u,r) F_2(u,r) ..., each F_i irreducible over S(r).
- Claim: all F_i have the same degree, and in all of them the same substitutions occur ('dieselben Substitutionen').
- My justification: let H = Gal(f / S(r)), a subgroup of G. The roots of F_1(u,r) are the images h(v) for h in H. Each other factor's roots form a coset of H, so every factor has degree |H| and the number of factors is [G:H].
- If r, r', ..., r^(n-1) are all the conjugates of r over S, the identity F(u) = Π F_i(u,r) is a polynomial identity in r modulo the minimal polynomial of r. Hence F(u) = Π F_i(u,r') for each conjugate r'.
- My addition: each F_i(u,r') is irreducible over S(r'), via the isomorphism S(r) ≅ S(r').
- The next page develops this into the reciprocal decomposition: f irreducible, φ 'normal' (its roots rational in any one root); f splits over S(ρ) into k factors and φ splits over S(r) into k factors.

Right column, 'Allgemeiner Satz':
- Let S_1, S_2, ... be fields each containing the coefficients of f, with groups G_1, G_2, ... of f over them.
- Let G be their greatest common divisor, i.e. the intersection of the groups (roots labelled consistently in a common field).
- Claim: G is the group of f over the 'System S = S_1 S_2 ...'.
- In Dedekind's later usage the field generated by all the S_i (their 'Multiplum', the compositum) is meant; the group over the compositum is indeed contained in each G_i.
errors: The 'Allgemeiner Satz' (group over S_1 S_2 ... equals the intersection G_1 ∩ G_2 ∩ ...) is false in general if S_1 S_2 is the compositum. Only the inclusion Gal(f/S_1S_2) ⊆ G_1 ∩ G_2 holds. Counterexample: f = x^2 - 2, S_1 = Q(√3), S_2 = Q(√6). Then G_1 = G_2 = S_2 (order 2), but Q(√3,√6) contains √2, so the group over the compositum is trivial. If S_1 S_2 meant the intersection of fields, the inclusion goes the wrong way. Either way the statement needs extra hypotheses; it is stated without proof.
The intersection of the G_i is only meaningful once the roots are labelled consistently in a common field; this is left implicit.
Case 1 asserts equal degrees of the F_i 'natürlich' without proof. The claim is correct (coset argument), but unjustified on the page.

results.what: Program: reduction of the Galois group to a subgroup by adjunction (extension of the base field), with the two main cases of adjoining one root of an irreducible equation and adjoining a normal ('vollständig') system
results.modern_name: Galois group under base extension; Galois Propositions II/III; normal extensions
results.usually_credited_to: Galois (1831); systematized by Jordan (1870), Dedekind's Göttingen lectures 1856–58

results.what: Over S(r), r a root of an irreducible equation, the Galois resolvent splits into irreducible factors of equal degree, each with the same group; conjugating r gives the analogous factorizations
results.modern_name: Galois resolvent factors correspond to cosets of Gal(f/S(r)) in Gal(f/S)

results.what: Group of f over the composite of fields S_1, S_2, ... equals the intersection of the groups G_i
results.modern_name: Galois group over a compositum (only containment Gal(f/K1K2) ⊆ Gal(f/K1) ∩ Gal(f/K2) holds in general)
results.usually_credited_to: folklore; no standard attribution (the equality is false in general)

deep.surprise_reason: This belongs to Dedekind's well-known Galois-theory lecture notes of 1856–58 (studied by Purkert and Scharlau). Base extension, resolvent factorization and normal adjunction follow Galois. The only notable item is an overgeneral (false) claim about groups over a compositum: a minor slip, not a discovery.

checkable.asserts: x^2-2 stays irreducible over Q(√3), so G_1 has order 2
x^2-2 stays irreducible over Q(√6), so G_2 has order 2
x^2-2 splits over Q(√3,√6), so the group over the compositum is trivial, not G_1 ∩ G_2 (counterexample to the Allgemeiner Satz)
a Galois resolvent of x^3-2 over Q has degree 6 = |S_3|
Case 1: adjoining one root r = 2^(1/3) splits the resolvent into 3 irreducible factors, all of degree 2
Case 2 (normal adjunction): the resolvent splits into 2 factors of equal degree 3

transcription_corrections: The 'Allgemeiner Satz' reads more like 'Gebiete, in deren jedem die Coefficienten ... enthalten sind' (not 'in denen jeden').
Title: the struck word and its replacement are uncertain; 'Verminderung' is plausible but not secure.
'in allen sind ups[?], die dieselben Substitutionen' is uncertain. It plausibly says that the same substitutions occur in all factors (perhaps 'in allen sind uns die dieselben ...').
The small superscript marks after S_1 ('S_1^r', 'S_1^5' in the image) appear to be insertion/reference marks, not exponents.
